bp.ADSR.name: bp.ADSR

Attack - time taken for initial level increase from zero to peak, beginning when the gate is first received.

Sustain - level during the stage following the decay stage.

Release - time taken for the level to decay from the sustain level to zero after the gate is released.

bp.ADSR2.name: bp.ADSR2
bp.ADSR2.digest:
Attack time is the time taken for initial run-up of level from nil to peak, beginning when the key or gate is first recieved.

Decay time is the time taken for the subsequent run down from the attack level to the designated sustain level.

Sustain level is the level during the main sequence of the sound's duration, until the key is released.

Release time is the time taken for the level to decay from the sustain level to zero after the key is released.
bp.ADSR2.description:

Release time is the time taken for the level to decay from the sustain level to zero after the key is released.

bp.Compressor.name: bp.Compressor
bp.Compressor.digest:
Threshold
A compressor reduces the level of an audio signal if its amplitude exceeds a certain threshold. It is commonly set in decibels dB, where a lower threshold (e.g. -60 dB) means a larger portion of the signal will be treated (compared to a higher threshold of e.g. −5 dB).

Ratio
The amount of gain reduction is determined by ratio: a ratio of 4:1 means that if input level is 4 dB over the threshold, the output signal level will be 1 dB over the threshold. The gain (level) has been reduced by 3 dB:

Threshold = −10 dB
The highest ratio of ∞:1 is often known as 'limiting'. It is commonly achieved using a ratio of 60:1, and effectively denotes that any signal above the threshold will be brought down to the threshold level (except briefly after a sudden increase in input loudness, known as an "attack").

Attack and Release
A compressor might provide a degree of control over how quickly it acts. The 'attack phase' is the period when the compressor is decreasing gain to reach the level that is determined by the ratio. The 'release phase' is the period when the compressor is increasing gain to the level determined by the ratio, or, to zero dB, once the level has fallen below the threshold.

Select an image from the preset menu, or import an image using the import button. Adjust the brightness and contrast settings to further refine the image data. 

Adjust the Position control to change the location in the filter - this will use the vertical data at that point in the image to create a filter contour. The contour is displayed at the top of the module in either linear or logarithmic scaling.

The Position can be modulated using the Position CV input.

bp.Sync Delay.name: bp.Sync Delay
bp.Sync Delay.digest:
The Sync Delay creates a stereo pair of signals out of a single incoming signal. You select the delay time for each channel in musical duration values using the two drop-down menus.

The feedback control sets the amount of feedback within the delay line - with high levels creating overwhelming levels of feedback. The HPF (High Pass Filter) and LPF (Low Pass Filter) allow you to contour the sound of the delay.

The Mix control sets the blend of direct and delayed signal.

The Mix control sets the blend of direct and delayed signal.
